correctness.rationale: Kaymakçalan–Selçuk Theorem 3 applies on the closed bi-infinite opportunity set with immediate on-clock reset and constant input. Equivalently, after the reset the unreset branch is exactly the exponential in elapsed physical time, so the first permitted threshold event is the non-strict forward projection of t+T_c. If T_c=qP+r with r=0, each phase returns after qP with q≥1. For 0<r<P, phase 0 switches after qP+a iff r≤a and otherwise repeats after (q+1)P; phase a switches after qP+b iff r≤b and otherwise repeats after (q+1)P. Both switches produce a two-spike interval sum of (2q+1)P; otherwise a fixed phase is reached within one step, or both phases are fixed. This proves initial-phase independence of the physical-time rate including exact equalities. The uniform reference gives 2/[P ceil(2T_c/P)]; strict loss occurs exactly for min(a,b)<r≤P/2. At T_c=P/2, high rate requires both gaps at least P/2, which forces uniformity; the rates are then 2/P versus 1/P. The frozen VERIFICATION.md and exact rational checker were inspected but not executed. The finite test set does not certify all positive real parameters; the phase calculation does. The finding does not apply to inserted continuous crossing times, stochastic jitter, or periodic input generally.

evidence: Set α=a/P and s=r/P∈(0,1). Insert α+ε just after α. The only threshold targets for the old phases, modulo one, are s and α+s. Choose ε>0 so neither target belongs to (α,α+ε] modulo one; a target exactly at α is unaffected by inclusive thresholding. Thus from both original initial phases the projected iterates remain exactly unchanged, including at boundaries.

For sufficiently small ε<s the sorted smallest gap is ε and c=max(α,1−α−ε)≥1/2 (when α=1/2, the unchanged α is a largest gap). The earlier comparison table gives rate 2 iff s≤1−c, otherwise 1. Here 1−c lies between min(α,1−α) and min(α,1−α)+ε. If s is strictly above that minimum, also take ε smaller than the margin. This gives exactly the closed high-rate regime and the low-rate complement. Return to general q by adding q whole periods per iterate: normalized reduced rate ρ becomes ρ/[P(1+qρ)].
